title: Winganhauppauge (Champlain's Creek)
summary: Winganhauppauge is an Islip placename tied to a neck of land and brook also associated with Champlain's Creek.
introduction_content: Winganhauppauge is a neck of land and brook in Islip, with forms including Wingan Hauppauge, Winganhoppog, Wingatt, and the cross-reference form Wingatthappagh.
history_content: The name appears in colonial land records for the Islip area and was connected with the brook or its headwaters before later interpretations attached to the broader place.
translation_content:
A common free interpretation is "Pleasant Springs," but the stronger reading is a water-place meaning connected with flooded or overflowed land. Wingatthappagh is treated as a cross-reference form of the same name.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names teach you how to respect the land.”

— Christine Schreyer, Jon Corbett, Nicole Gordon, and Colleen Larson, Learning to talk to the land: Online stewardship in Taku River Tlingit territory (2014), abstract, four educational themes
preservation_content: Several Islip-area spellings are kept together here, with the location marked as approximate so the placename remains visible without implying an exact historical boundary.
whereintheworld_content: Approximate blue/general placement in Islip near the Champlain's Creek area. Coordinates are a modern approximate anchor and are not exact historic coordinates.
